messages.content: Predict the human participant’s choice or report in this anonymous laboratory game. Roles A and B remain fixed for 11 rounds; A and B are randomly rematched after each round. Each round A starts with EUR16 and B with EUR8. A sends either EUR0 or EUR8 to B. B independently commits a conditional punishment cost c from EUR0 to EUR4 in EUR0.1 steps, without observing A’s current choice: if A sends EUR0, A earns 16-4c and B earns 8-c; if A sends EUR8, A earns8 and B earns16 and c is not implemented. Both learn their interaction outcome after confirming their decisions and answering a belief question. One round is selected for payment independently for each person, plus EUR4 show-up pay. Communication is prohibited. In this treatment, after the first interaction all Bs simultaneously choose peer punishment. Bs see the current conditional costs of all Bs sorted from highest to lowest and their own marked row. A B can target only Bs with strictly lower conditional cost; self, equal and higher costs cannot be targeted. Allocate up to EUR4 total across eligible targets, in EUR0.1 steps. Each EUR0.1 spent removes EUR0.4 from that target. Own expenditure is removed before incoming punishment; incoming reductions add and final earnings cannot fall below zero. A is unaffected by this stage. Output only your chosen transfer amount, 0 or8, in EUR.

You are PersonA, in round1 of11, with 10 As and 10 Bs in this session. A and B see the past session mean conditional punishment history; B additionally faces peer punishment. Group history below uses the on-screen aggregate reduction of A earnings in EUR, rounded to one decimal, not the unrounded mean; the cost behind a reduction is one quarter as large. All Bs can observe peer conditional strategies after first-stage decisions; only past strategies appear before a new strategy choice. Ranked rows are not stable peer identities. Earlier recorded actions and visible feedback are provided below; practice actions were not released, which does not mean the participant did not experience them. Reported stable attributes: sex female, author-recorded age 20 years; measured in postexperiment demographics.
